Fixes #338949

## Summary

- Apply custom agents' authored model and supported reasoning-effort defaults through existing per-chat selection, keeping the picker and requests aligned.
- Preserve ordered model alternatives through discovery and chat modes. Read authored effort on the host when the runtime's discovery response omits it.
- Keep later explicit model choices authoritative without writing agent defaults to shared preferences.

The shared chat-input changes also affect regular local Copilot Chat. Host-owned inputs retain their existing selection ownership.

## Validation

Rebased onto current `main`; the following checks passed afterward:

```sh
pnpm run build-fast --client-only
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentMetaReaders.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/test/common/pluginParsers.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputModelSelectionController.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatModeService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptFileParser.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts \
  --reporter dot
pnpm run typecheck-client
git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 pnpm run eslint
```

Results: client build passed; **1,075 tests passed, 11 pending**; typecheck and changed-file ESLint passed.

### Live Code OSS verification

Verified this worktree before the conflict-free rebase, with dbgjs attached to the local Copilot agent host. A temporary agent declared `model: claude-sonnet-5.5` and `reasoning-effort: low`, starting from a Luna/Medium picker selection:

| Action | Picker / runtime configuration | Actual response model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select agent and send first turn | Sonnet / Low | `claude-sonnet-5.5` |
| Send follow-up | Sonnet / Low | `claude-sonnet-5.5` |
| Explicitly choose Luna and send | Luna / Medium | `gpt-6-luna` |
| Clear and reselect agent, then send | Sonnet / Low | `claude-sonnet-5.5` |

dbgjs logpoints verified create-time and follow-up model/effort; runtime journals verified response models. Live verification covered the Agents window, not regular local Chat or remote/cloud hosts. Automated tests cover regular input selection and opaque host-authored agent metadata.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new read, its placement inside the loop, and the awaited session-publication call path are explicit. Runtime omission is both the stated compatibility case and covered by the added test. Exact delay varies with agent count and filesystem latency, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem reads and frontmatter parsing CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N non-builtin agents whose discovery response omits reasoningEffort, discovery now performs N file reads serially because each await is inside the loop; plugin agents may also be read again by parsePlugin/readAgentComponents later in the same discovery.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased customization/session initialization latency and slower refreshes, especially with many agents or slow/network-mounted filesystems.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: discoverAgents awaited the single agents.discover RPC and projected its result without reading each agent file; plugin parsing remained the only file-parse path for plugin agents.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each non-builtin agent missing reasoningEffort now blocks the loop on parseAgentFile, which calls IFileService.readFile and parses the full frontmatter before the next agent is processed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added expression `agent.reasoningEffort ?? (await parseAgentFile(uri, this._fileService)).reasoningEffort` at line 610 introduces the per-agent read and serial await; the deleted implementation had no filesystem operation in this loop.
Findings.Title: Batch fallback agent-file reads during discovery
Findings.Impact: Creating a session for a new anchor waits through getCustomizationsSettled -> SessionDiscoveredEntry.whenSettled -> discover, so an older runtime that omits this field adds one serialized filesystem round trip per discovered agent before customizations can be published. Watched customization changes repeat the same fan-out after the 100 ms debounce.
Findings.Evidence: SessionCustomizationDiscovery.discover awaits discoverAgents in its discovery Promise.all. discoverAgents loops the runtime result and the changed line awaits parseAgentFile for every missing value. parseAgentFile immediately awaits fileService.readFile. SessionDiscoveredEntry._refresh awaits discover, while SessionPluginController.getCustomizationsSettled/getAppliedCustomizations await the entry's whenSettled before session publication/application. toPluginCustomizations subsequently calls parsePlugin, whose readAgentComponents reads plugin agent files again.
Findings.Recommendation: Collect agents first and resolve all missing-effort fallbacks concurrently with a bounded/shared parse pass (for example, Promise.all over missing entries, reusing plugin parse results where applicable), then preserve result order when projecting them. Cache by URI/etag across refreshes if reads cannot be shared.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or refresh a Copilot agent-host session and discover workspace, user, and plugin custom agents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionPluginController.getCustomizationsSettled/getAppliedCustomizations waits for SessionDiscoveredEntry.whenSettled, whose refresh awaits SessionCustomizationDiscovery.discover and therefore discoverAgents before customizations are published or applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK agents.discover request for all project paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped RPC per discovery refresh, independent of agent count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single grouped discovery RPC was awaited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before agent projection and the settled customization snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse each agent markdown file to recover reasoning-effort
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial read for every non-builtin discovered agent whose runtime result lacks reasoningEffort; effective cardinality is N missing-field agents. Plugin agents can be read again by the existing plugin parse pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: discoverAgents performed no per-agent file read; plugin files were read only by the existing plugin parse path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each read blocks the next loop iteration and completion of discovery, directly extending initial session customization publication and refresh latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Locate plugin roots and parse plugin manifests/components
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing work grouped by unique plugin root, with component reads inside parsePlugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin discovery already performed this work once per unique plugin root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited after parallel top-level discovery; the new fallback can duplicate an agent-file read before this pass.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered non-builtin agents missing runtime effort metadata after SDK grouping; no deduplication or cache is applied to the new fallback reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The top-level discovery categories run in Promise.all, but fallback agent reads are serialized at concurrency 1 by await inside the for-loop. Refreshes are coalesced by a 100 ms Delayer and one anchor instance is shared for identical anchor sets.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered directories are cached and anchors share one discovery instance, but parsed agent contents/reasoning effort are not cached by URI or etag. Every watcher-triggered or explicit refresh repeats all missing-field reads; no negative or warm content cache is visible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the introduced filesystem read, serial placement, repeated refresh path, and settled-session dependency are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent counts and local filesystem latency vary, but older runtimes explicitly omit the field and network-mounted workspaces make serialized round trips realistically visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity I/O boundary fan-out on the session customization critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select or reselect a custom agent in a draft or running agent-host chat and apply its model/reasoning preference
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection synchronously resolves published agent metadata and scans the in-memory model catalogue; running chats then use the pre-existing asynchronous chat-state update before UI state converges, while send requests consume the selected model/configuration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of draft sessions on a model-catalogue event, published/client agents during identity resolution, model alternatives, and registered models. Typical effective cardinality is one active draft, a small preference list, and one model catalogue.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model-change events synchronously iterate all draft sessions; per-draft reconciliation is serialized in-process. Configuration writes added for agent defaults pass persist=false, so they do not call the shared language-model persistence service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The per-draft agentModelPreferenceApplied flag coalesces repeated catalogue events after a preference resolves and resets only when the agent source changes; unresolved preferences retry when model events arrive. Running-session preference resolution is performed once per explicit agent change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the new work is in-memory and bounded by active drafts/models; the existing acquireOrLoadSession/update path was already invoked by setAgent before the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large numbers of simultaneous drafts or models are uncommon, and no expensive external boundary was found in the added reconciliation work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression beyond the discovery finding: catalogue scans and draft iteration are bounded, and persistence I/O is explicitly suppressed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate a regular/local chat custom mode and align the input model picker and reasoning configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A reactive mode effect reads model preferences/effort, scans the input's current in-memory model pool, updates the per-input configuration store, and applies the programmatic selection before the next request.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authored model-alternative count multiplied by the number of models in the current input pool; both are small user/configuration collections and resolution stops at the first match.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-side resolution on mode/model observable changes; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is used, but the operation runs only when observed mode/model state changes. Configuration is restored with persist=false and merged with the current per-input configuration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper implementations only allocate a small catalogue and scan arrays; no expensive boundary is transitively reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact model-pool sizes vary by provider, but there is no realistic large collection or high-frequency frame/input loop in the traced path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; added synchronous work is small and event-bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Parse custom-agent/plugin files and cache their model and reasoning metadata in chat modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing file discovery reads markdown components, parses frontmatter, and constructs metadata before modes are cached or projected to the picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read agent markdown components during plugin/customization parsing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing read per discovered markdown component, issued concurrently with Promise.all after component enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same files were read and parsed for name, description, model, tools, and invocation flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete for plugin parsing as before; the added metadata fields are extracted from the already parsed frontmatter and do not add another read on this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and size of discovered agent markdown files; the diff adds only small arrays/strings to already-created customization and mode objects.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: readAgentComponents parses files concurrently with Promise.all, then deduplicates/sorts in memory.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat mode objects retain the added model alternatives and one effort string alongside existing metadata; lifecycle remains tied to the existing mode/customization cache and update observables.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that parser work reuses existing file contents/frontmatter and retained metadata is bounded per live agent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authored model lists could vary, but realistic lists are short and no unbounded history or new cache key is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: metadata propagation adds negligible bounded allocation; duplicate plugin reads are attributable to the reported discovery fallback.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 20 changed files. One introduced boundary-fanout issue was reported: serialized per-agent fallback file reads on settled session discovery. Model selection, reactive input updates, persistence suppression, cache lifecycles, and parser metadata propagation were traced and did not establish additional actionable regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
